Definition: from G1484; national ("ethnic"), i.e. (specially) a Gentile:--heathen (man).
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, ethnikós means national, that is a Gentile. Most of its 4 occurrences are in Matthew. The word does quiet work, and the passages below show it in its ordinary setting.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: ethnikós means what it says, and what it says matters. It is a small word with a steady job, and I trust it to do that job.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Diotrephes Refuses the Brethren
